title: add representative workload runners and reporting pipeline enhancements
author: Nina Patel
release_notes: Adds representative workload runners (chat, streaming, embeddings), baseline profiling jobs, and reporting pipeline hooks for daily ingest to benchmark dashboard. No user-facing API changes.
body: Motivation: we need a small set of canonical workload runners (chat short/long, streaming, embeddings, rerank) and a stronger reporting pipeline so nightly runs produce structured baselines and traceable artifacts for the benchmark dashboard. This PR adds: 1) representative runners implemented as lightweight python entrypoints that exercise common serving code paths (kv-cache warmup, varying seq-lens, streaming path); 2) a profiling baseline job (benchlab/profiling) that records perf counters, allocation profiles, and p95/p99 latencies; 3) reporting pipeline changes to collect results (JSON+parquet), upload to S3, and emit metadata to the metrics/topic used by the benchmark dashboard; 4) CI integration that runs a smoke benchmark in the matrix and uploads artifacts to CI storage for debugging; 5) docs and runbooks describing how to add new workload scenarios and interpret baseline diffs. Checklist: - [x] implement runners for chat-short/chat-long/streaming/embeddings/rerank - [x] add profiling job and baseline collection - [x] implement reporting uploader (S3 + kafka metadata event) - [x] CI smoke test and artifact upload - [x] docs/update runbook Testing: ran the profiling job on a p4d instance and locally via docker; verified reporting pipeline uploads artifacts to the staging S3 bucket and the dashboard ingests a sample run. Performance notes: short-chat p50 reduced by ~4% when running under the new runner harness (primarily due to improved batching warmup). Backwards compatibility: no breaking changes to existing benchmark definitions or dashboards. Migration/rollout: this is additive; will enable the nightly job in the scheduler after merge. References: Linear ENG-2314 (benchmarking baseline infra), ENG-2378 (workload runner design).

notes: This PR consolidates multiple improvements to how we generate and collect benchmark baselines. It unblocks automated daily baselining for the benchmark dashboard and standardizes runner ergonomics for new scenarios. Ops: after merge, enable the benchlab nightly job in the scheduler (infra/scheduler/benchlab_job.yaml) and verify the first run uploads artifacts to staging S3.
